text: ivd implements Spike--Slab Mixed-Effects Location Scale Model (SS-MELSM, Carmo et al. 2026) detect heterogeneous residual variances hierarchical data. standard mixed-effects models assume constant within-group variability, mixed-effects location scale models explicitly models residual variance function covariates random effects. SS-MELSM uses spike--slab prior probabilistically identify specific units (e.g., schools, individuals) exhibit unusually high low consistency, distinguishing population average.

ivd() fits SS-MELSM lme4-style formulas location scale sub-models; chains run parallel, grouping IDs (character, factor, non-consecutive numeric codes) accepted. summary() plot() report unit’s posterior inclusion probability (PIP), PIP, funnel, outcome plots; results can labelled original grouping IDs (labels = "original"). pip(), fixef(), ranef(), coef() extract tidy estimates processing. pip_sensitivity() shows PIPs – resulting classifications – change different prior inclusion probabilities, computed analytically without refitting. pip_fdr() selects deviant units controlling Bayesian false discovery rate instead arbitrary fixed PIP cutoff, pip_diagnostics() reports PIP’s Monte Carlo error -chain agreement. pp_check() runs posterior predictive check within-cluster SDs, family = "student" provides robust t likelihood heavy tails mistaken variance heterogeneity. title: ivd (development version)
text: Two new vignettes: Interpreting posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs, decision rules, prior sensitivity, Monte Carlo diagnostics, simulation known deviant clusters) Convergence robustness (spike--slab convergence pitfalls, heavy tails masquerade variance heterogeneity – student-t remedy). New chains argument ivd(), decoupled workers: chains distributed worker processes, worker compiles model reuses chains – extra chains cost sampling time additional compilation. chains defaults workers, preserving behaviour (exact draws) existing code. summary() now labels count “Chains:” instead “Chains (workers):”. New family = "student" option ivd(): student-t likelihood estimated degrees freedom (nu = 2 + gamma(shape, rate), reported nu summary(); prior tunable via priors = list(nu = ...)). Heavy tails can masquerade variance heterogeneity gaussian likelihood, inflating PIPs clusters merely contain outliers – "student" absorbs tails instead. pp_check(), WAIC/logLik, plots simulate_ivd() (via family/df arguments) support . New simulate_ivd(): simulates data intercept-MELSM known subset clusters whose within-cluster SD inflated (deflated) chosen factor. Returns data ready ivd() plus ground truth per cluster – power analysis, teaching, recovery checks. New pp_check() method: posterior predictive check within-cluster SDs – quantity spike--slab makes claims . Default view compares cluster’s observed SD predictive interval (outliers highlighted labelled); type = "density" overlays observed cluster-SD density replicated ones. Systematic misfit suggests normal likelihood inadequate (e.g. heavy tails). New priors argument ivd(): prior hyperparameters – location intercept coefficients (normal), scale coefficients (normal), random-effect SDs (half-t df/scale), LKJ shape – can now set user, e.g. priors = list(zeta = c(sd = 1), lkj_eta = 2). Partial specifications filled (unchanged) defaults, resolved specification stored fit $priors. New pip_diagnostics(): Monte Carlo diagnostics PIPs, binary-indicator Rhat cover. Reports per-chain PIPs, Monte Carlo standard error pooled PIP, flags clusters whose classification pip_level differs chains (.e. PIPs trusted without iterations). New pip_fdr(): Bayesian false-discovery-rate decision rule selecting deviant clusters (Newton et al., 2004). Instead fixed PIP cutoff, selects largest cluster set whose expected FDR stays target level reports implied, data-adaptive PIP threshold (usable pip_level plot()). Ecosystem bridges: .mcmc.list() (coda) as_draws() (posterior) convert fit standard formats human-readable parameter labels used summary(), opening bayesplot/tidybayes/posterior tooling (e.g. bayesplot::mcmc_trace(.mcmc.list(fit), pars = "Intc")). ivd() accepts arbitrary grouping IDs (character, factor, numeric gaps, e.g. real school codes). IDs recoded internally 1..J index NIMBLE needs – without reordering data – original labels stored fitted object group_labels. summary() plot() gained shared labels = c("index", "original") argument: default keeps compact internal cluster index displays; "original" switches user’s grouping IDs. New print() method fitted objects: formulas, data dimensions, sampling setup, one-line convergence note (max split-Rhat, min n_eff). New pip() extractor returning posterior inclusion probabilities tidy data frame (one row per cluster x scale random effect, original cluster IDs). New fixef(), ranef(), coef() extractors following lme4/nlme conventions (without adding dependency either). New pip_sensitivity(): analytic prior-sensitivity PIPs. posterior odds converted prior-independent Bayes factor re-weighted across grid prior inclusion probabilities – refit needed. Comes plot() method showing per-cluster PIP trajectories (prior-sensitive clusters highlighted; subset clusters =). summary() now returns structured summary.ivd object ($table, $waic, $lppd, $pwaic, $chains) rendered separate print() method; console output unchanged.
